children.text: High School students at SAIS Abu Dhabi experience increased independence, responsibility, and engagement throughout their academic journey. Our High School program offers students a diverse range of elective and advanced courses that allow them to explore their interests, discover their strengths, and connect their learning to future university studies and career aspirations.
Students are encouraged to think critically, communicate effectively, solve problems creatively, and develop the confidence needed to succeed in a rapidly changing world.

heading.title: Freedom to Explore, Guidance to Grow

image.alt: Freedom to Explore, Guidance to Grow

children.text: The High School program emphasizes student-centered learning, inquiry, collaboration, and meaningful real-world applications of knowledge. Through rigorous academic experiences, project-based learning, leadership opportunities, research, presentations, and collaborative activities, students develop essential academic, personal, and social skills.

With continuous guidance and personalized support from teachers and counselors, students are empowered to become active learners, responsible individuals, and well-prepared graduates who are ready for higher education, future careers, and lifelong success.

The High School curriculum at SAIS Abu Dhabi is designed to provide students with a flexible and enriching academic experience that supports their individual interests, strengths, and future goals. Through Advanced Placement (AP) courses, elective options, and career guidance opportunities, students are encouraged to explore different fields of study while preparing for university and future careers.

Our curriculum emphasizes college and career readiness, critical thinking, leadership, entrepreneurship, creativity, and interdisciplinary learning. Students are provided with opportunities to develop academically, socially, and personally through engaging learning experiences that prepare them to become confident, responsible, and successful global citizens.

Career guidance empowers students to make informed, careful, and personalized choices for higher education and career readiness. Our program supports students in academic planning, course selection, goal setting, career exploration, soft-skills development, and post-secondary transition, including admissions processes.
Our Career Guidance curriculum develops higher education and career readiness through these key themes:
Academic & Skill Based Exploration and Strategic Planning
Meta-Cognitive, Transition, and Soft Skills Development
Financial Literacy, Personal Accountability, and Goal Setting
Our courses provide students with opportunities to explore different fields of study and career interests while preparing for higher education and future careers.

These courses help students build knowledge, practical skills, critical thinking, creativity, communication, and problem-solving abilities. They also guide students in making informed decisions about university majors and career choices, serving as an educational roadmap that connects high school learning with future academic and professional goals.

children.text: Advanced Placement (AP) is a College Board program that allows high school students to take courses that can earn college credits and/or qualify them for advanced university classes. AP courses are weighted (1.25) provided students achieve qualifying scores on the respective College Board Exam.
AP classes are optional. All enrolled students must sit for the College Board AP exam and cover the cost of required resources and exams.
We offer a range of Advanced Placement (AP) courses designed to challenge students academically and prepare them for higher education.
AP courses provide students with college-level learning experiences that strengthen critical thinking, analytical skills, research abilities, and academic readiness for university studies.
